clauses.clause: para. 1: creates a three-member emergency board, appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; members must be disinterested
para. 2: board shall report its findings to the President within thirty days
para. 3: no change in the conditions of the dispute, except by agreement, from the order date until thirty days after the board's report
clauses.end: 1950-09-10 (30 days after the 1950-08-11 report); formally revoked 1986-02-25

data_errors: Tracker blocker FIRST_END_UNRESOLVED can be cleared: the board's report is dated 1950-08-11 (NMB PEB 87/88 report, public web, not held in the repository), so the own-terms end is 1950-09-10.
The report is dated 1950-08-11, more than thirty days after the 1950-07-03 order; no extension of the reporting deadline was looked for. This does not affect status.
EO 12553's list describes EO 10138 as a 'railroad labor dispute'; the carrier is a dock company under the Railway Labor Act. Descriptive only; the number is the identifier.

moves.note: Federal Register printing at 15 FR 4241 is held and legible; three operative clauses listed.
NO. Order ran out under its own terms in 1950 (report made 1950-08-11) and was expressly revoked by number in EO 12553, 1986-02-25.
Each of the three clauses has an end date and a source.
No open gap. The 1950-09-10 end is computed as 30 days from the transmittal date printed on the report; the express 1986 revocation is the backstop.

propositions.claim: EO 10138 is printed in the Federal Register of July 4, 1950, signed July 3, 1950.
propositions.quote: EXECUTIVE ORDER 10138 Creating an Emergency Board To Investigate Dispute Between the Toledo, Lorain & Fairport Dock Company and Certain of Its Employees

propositions.claim: The order creates a three-member board to investigate the dispute.
propositions.quote: I hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to investigate the said dispute.

propositions.claim: The board must report to the President within thirty days.
propositions.quote: The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to the said dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.

propositions.claim: The status-quo command ends by its own terms thirty days after the board's report.
propositions.quote: from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made

propositions.claim: The board appointed under EO 10138 and 10139 issued a report to the President dated August 11, 1950.
propositions.quote: Report to the President by the Emergency Board appointed July 3, 1950, by Executive Orders 10138 and 10139 ... Toledo, Ohio August 11, 1950

propositions.claim: The board submitted its report to the President by letter of transmittal dated August 11, 1950.
propositions.quote: Toledo, Ohio, August 11, 1950. ... The Emergency Board appointed by you on July 3, 1950 ... has the honor to submit herewith its report.

propositions.claim: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986 revokes a list of executive orders as no longer necessary.
propositions.quote: to eliminate Executive Orders that are no longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked

propositions.claim: EO 10138 is named by number in the EO 12553 revocation list.
propositions.quote: 10138 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute

review.conclusion_reason: The August 11 report supports completion of the investigation and reporting duties; the original's thirty-day post-report limit supports September 10, 1950 as the operative ending. EO 12553 independently establishes express formal revocation on February 25, 1986. Every listed clause is ended before the cutoff.
missed_evidence: The cited NMB report, PDF page 6 (printed page 4), expressly confirms the President extended the reporting deadline: 'extended the date of our report to not later than September 1, 1950.' This resolves the worker's observation about the report exceeding the original thirty-day deadline. Source: https://nmb.gov/NMB_Application/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/PEB-088-Report.pdf

verdicts.reason: Held Federal Register text identifies EO 10138, publication July 4, 1950, and signature July 3, 1950.
Held original contains the quoted three-member board creation and investigation command, followed by the member-disinterest requirement.
Held original expressly requires reporting within thirty days from the order date.
Held original expressly limits the status-quo command to thirty days after the board reports, with an exception for agreement.
NMB report cover identifies Executive Orders 10138 and 10139 and bears August 11, 1950.
NMB report PDF page 2 contains the August 11, 1950 transmittal to the President submitting the report for the named dock-company disputes.
Held EO 12553 printing identifies February 25, 1986 and expressly revokes the listed orders and their amendments as no longer necessary.
Held EO 12553 text at 51 FR 7238 explicitly lists 10138 with the quoted railroad-labor-dispute description.
